debutant.question: To which sea did Moses lead the Israelites when leaving Egypt?
debutant.explanation: Moses parted the Red Sea to allow the Israelites to flee Pharaoh's army (Exodus 14).

debutant.question: In which city was Jesus born?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, according to the prophecy of Micah 5:2 (Matthew 2:1).

debutant.question: In which town did Jesus grow up?
debutant.explanation: Jesus grew up in Nazareth of Galilee, which is why he was called 'Jesus of Nazareth' (Luke 2:51).

debutant.question: On which mountain did Moses receive the Ten Commandments?
debutant.explanation: Moses received the Ten Commandments from God on Mount Sinai (Exodus 20).

debutant.question: What river did John the Baptist use to baptize?
debutant.explanation: John the Baptist baptized in the Jordan, and it was there that Jesus was baptized (Matthew 3:13).

debutant.question: In which garden was Jesus arrested?
debutant.explanation: Jesus prayed and was arrested in the Garden of Gethsemane, at the foot of the Mount of Olives (Matthew 26:36).

debutant.question: To which country did Abraham receive God's call to go?
debutant.explanation: Abraham (Abram) received the divine call to Ur from the Chaldeans in Mesopotamia (Genesis 11:31; Acts 7:2-4).

debutant.question: What country did the Israelites leave during the Exodus?
debutant.explanation: The Exodus is the exit of the Hebrew people from Egypt under the leadership of Moses (Exodus 12-15).

debutant.question: On which mountain did Noah's ark rest after the flood?
debutant.explanation: Noah's ark rested on the Ararat Mountains (Genesis 8:4).

debutant.question: In which city was Paul converted along the way?
debutant.explanation: Paul (Saul) had his vision of the resurrected Christ on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:3).

debutant.question: On which island did John write the Apocalypse?
debutant.explanation: John received the visions of Revelation while exiled on the island of Patmos (Revelation 1:9).

debutant.question: In which sea was Paul shipwrecked?
debutant.explanation: Paul was shipwrecked near the island of Malta in the Mediterranean Sea (Acts 27-28).

debutant.question: In which city did Solomon build the Temple?
debutant.explanation: Solomon built the first Temple on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem (1 Kings 6).

debutant.question: Where was Abraham willing to sacrifice Isaac?
debutant.explanation: God had asked Abraham to go to the land of Moriah to offer Isaac (Genesis 22:2).

debutant.question: What is the main inland Sea of ​​Galilee?
debutant.explanation: Lake Tiberias, also called the Sea of ​​Galilee or Lake Gennesaret, was the center of Jesus' ministry in Galilee.

debutant.question: In which city did Mary live when the angel Gabriel announced to her the birth of Jesus?
debutant.explanation: The angel Gabriel was sent to Nazareth, a town in Galilee, to Mary (Luke 1:26-27).

debutant.question: In which city is the pool of Siloam where Jesus healed a man born blind?
debutant.explanation: Jesus sent the man born blind to wash in the pool of Siloam in Jerusalem (John 9:7).

debutant.question: Which city was destroyed along with Sodom by fire and brimstone?
debutant.explanation: God rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah because of their sin (Genesis 19:24).

debutant.question: To which city was Jonah sent by God to preach repentance?
debutant.explanation: God sent Jonah to Nineveh, the great capital of Assyria (Jonah 1:2; 3:2).

debutant.question: On what mountain was Jesus crucified just outside the walls of Jerusalem?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was crucified at a place called Golgotha, which means 'place of the Skull' (John 19:17).

debutant.question: In which village did Lazarus, Martha and Mary, Jesus' friends, live?
debutant.explanation: Lazarus, Martha, and Mary lived in Bethany, near Jerusalem (John 11:1).

debutant.question: In which town in Galilee did Jesus perform his first miracle at a wedding?
debutant.explanation: Jesus changed water into wine at the wedding in Cana in Galilee (John 2:1-11).

debutant.question: Which river crosses Egypt and where the baby Moses was placed in a basket?
debutant.explanation: Moses' mother placed the basket of rushes among the reeds on the banks of the Nile (Exodus 2:3).

debutant.question: In which city did the walls collapse before the Israelites led by Joshua?
debutant.explanation: The walls of Jericho fell after the people had circumnavigated them (Joshua 6:20).

debutant.question: Which region of southern Israel was home to Jerusalem and Bethlehem in Jesus' time?
debutant.explanation: Jerusalem and Bethlehem are in Judea, in the south of the country (Matthew 2:1).

debutant.question: In which northern region did Jesus grow up and perform the majority of his miracles?
debutant.explanation: Jesus grew up in Nazareth and carried out most of his ministry in Galilee (Matthew 4:23).

debutant.question: What region was between Judea to the south and Galilee to the north?
debutant.explanation: Samaria was between Judea and Galilee; Jesus crossed it notably at Sychar (John 4:4).

debutant.question: What is the name of the hill east of Jerusalem where Jesus prayed and ascended into heaven?
debutant.explanation: The Mount of Olives faces the Temple in Jerusalem; this is where Gethsemane was located and the place of the Ascension (Acts 1:12).

debutant.question: Where did Moses see the burning bush that was not consumed?
options: On the banks of the Jordan
debutant.explanation: Moses was leading the flock to the mountain of God at Horeb when he saw the burning bush (Exodus 3:1-2).

debutant.question: On which mountain did Moses contemplate the Promised Land before dying?
debutant.explanation: Moses went up to Mount Nebo (summit of Pisgah) facing Jericho to see Canaan before his death (Deuteronomy 34:1).

debutant.question: In which city was Saul of Tarsus (the apostle Paul) born?
debutant.explanation: Paul himself declares himself to be 'a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia' (Acts 21:39).

debutant.question: In which city were the disciples first called 'Christians'?
debutant.explanation: It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians (Acts 11:26).

debutant.question: In which city did David establish his first capital for 7 years before Jerusalem?
debutant.explanation: David first reigned 7 years and 6 months in Hebron over Judah before conquering Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:5).

debutant.question: Where did the Israelites build the Tower that caused the confusion of languages?
debutant.explanation: Men built the tower in the plain of Shinar; the place was called Babel (Genesis 11:2-9).

debutant.question: In which desert did the Israelites live 40 years after the Exodus?
options: The desert of Sinai and Paran
The desert of central Saudi Arabia
debutant.explanation: They journeyed through the deserts of Shur, Sin, Sinai, Paran and Zin (Exodus, Numbers).

debutant.question: What village was about 7 miles from Jerusalem where the resurrected Jesus walked with two disciples?
debutant.explanation: Two disciples were on their way to the village of Emmaus when the resurrected Jesus walked with them (Luke 24:13).

debutant.question: In which city did Zacchaeus, the chief tax collector, climb a sycamore tree?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was passing through Jericho when He called Zacchaeus down from his sycamore tree (Luke 19:1-5).

debutant.question: What very salty sea is located at the southern end of the Jordan River?
debutant.explanation: The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea, also called the Salt Sea or Sea of ​​Araba in the Bible (Genesis 14:3).

debutant.question: In which city in Judea was David born and did he tend the flocks?
debutant.explanation: David was the son of Jesse of Bethlehem, also called the 'city of David' (1 Samuel 16:1; Luke 2:4).

debutant.question: What major city in the Roman Empire was the final destination of Paul's final journey in Acts?
debutant.explanation: Paul appealed to Caesar and was taken to Rome (Acts 28:14-16).

debutant.question: In which Greek city did Paul preach before the tribunal of the Areopagus?
debutant.explanation: Paul spoke to the Athenian philosophers in the middle of the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17:22).

debutant.question: Where was the prophet Daniel taken captive in his youth?
debutant.explanation: Daniel was deported to Babylon under King Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel 1:1-6).

debutant.question: In which city did Samson lose his strength and cause the temple of Dagon to collapse?
debutant.explanation: The Philistines imprisoned Samson in Gaza, where he overturned the pillars of the temple (Judges 16:21-30).

debutant.question: What country did the queen who came to test the wisdom of Solomon govern?
debutant.explanation: The Queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem with spices and gold to listen to Solomon (1 Kings 10:1).

debutant.question: In which city in northern Galilee did Peter and Andrew live during the time of Jesus' ministry?
debutant.explanation: Jesus often stayed in Capernaum, where Simon Peter's house was located (Mark 1:29; 2:1).

debutant.question: To what country did Abraham and Sarah go down when a famine struck Canaan?
debutant.explanation: A famine in Canaan caused Abraham to go to Egypt (Genesis 12:10).

debutant.question: On which mountain did the Israelites stand when Joshua renewed the Covenant between Ebal and Gerizim?
debutant.explanation: Moses then Joshua placed the tribes facing Mounts Gerizim (blessing) and Ebal (cursing) near Shechem (Joshua 8:33).

debutant.question: In which city did Jesus heal a paralytic who had fallen from a roof?
debutant.explanation: It was in Capernaum that four men opened the roof to lower the paralytic before Jesus (Mark 2:1-5).

debutant.question: Which river did Naaman the Syrian have to dive into 7 times to be cured of his leprosy?
debutant.explanation: Elisha ordered Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan (2 Kings 5:10-14).

debutant.question: In which port city did Jonah embark to flee to Tarshish?
debutant.explanation: Jonah went down to Jaffa (Joppa) and found a ship bound for Tarshish (Jonah 1:3).

debutant.question: In which city did Peter have the vision of the tablecloth coming down from heaven onto the terrace of Simon the leatherworker?
debutant.explanation: Peter was staying with Simon the leatherworker in Joppa when he received the vision before going to Cornelius (Acts 10:5-16).

debutant.question: In which city did the Roman centurion Cornelius baptized by Peter reside?
debutant.explanation: Cornelius, centurion of the so-called Italian cohort, resided in Caesarea Maritime (Acts 10:1).

debutant.question: What garden did God plant 'in Eden, on the east side' to place man there?
debutant.explanation: The LORD God planted a garden in Eden on the east side, and placed man there (Genesis 2:8).

debutant.question: In which city did Ruth and Naomi settle when returning from Moab?
debutant.explanation: Naomi and her daughter-in-law Ruth returned to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest (Ruth 1:22).

debutant.question: What country was Ruth's original homeland?
debutant.explanation: Ruth was a Moabite, from the land of Moab east of the Dead Sea (Ruth 1:4).

debutant.question: In which city did the first disciples meet in the 'upper room' at Pentecost?
debutant.explanation: Jesus had commanded the apostles not to depart from Jerusalem until the Father's promise (Acts 1:4; 2:1).

debutant.question: In which valley did David face Goliath?
options: The valley of Ela (of the Terebinths)
debutant.explanation: The Philistines and Israel camped opposite each other in the valley of Elah/Terebinths (1 Samuel 17:2).

debutant.question: Where did Jesus meet the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well?
debutant.explanation: Jesus stopped by Jacob's well at Sychar in Samaria (John 4:5-6).

debutant.question: What lake or sea borders the city of Capernaum?
debutant.explanation: Capernaum was located on the northwest shore of the Sea of ​​Galilee, also called Lake Gennesaret or Tiberias.

debutant.question: In which city in Asia Minor was the immense temple of Artemis which sparked a riot against Paul?
debutant.explanation: In Ephesus, the goldsmith Demetrius stirred up the crowd by shouting 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!' (Acts 19:28).

debutant.question: On which island did Paul shipwreck before reaching Rome?
debutant.explanation: After 14 days of storm, the ship ran aground on the island of Malta, where a viper bit Paul without harming him (Acts 28:1-5).

debutant.question: Which mountain dominates the southwest of Jerusalem and is often synonymous with the city of David?
debutant.explanation: David captured the stronghold of Zion, which became the city of David (2 Samuel 5:7).

intermediaire.question: What was the ancient name of the city of Jerusalem before its conquest by David?
intermediaire.explanation: Jerusalem was called Jebus, inhabited by the Jebusites, before being conquered by David (2 Samuel 5:6-9).

intermediaire.question: Between which two rivers was Mesopotamia located?
intermediaire.explanation: Mesopotamia (from the Greek: 'land between the rivers') is located between the Tigris and the Euphrates, in what is now Iraq.

intermediaire.question: In which city did Paul found the Church after 18 months of stay?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul stayed 18 months in Corinth during his 2nd missionary journey to found the Church there (Acts 18:11).

intermediaire.question: What was the capital of the Northern Kingdom (Israel)?
intermediaire.explanation: Samaria was built by King Omri as the capital of the Northern Kingdom (1 Kings 16:24).

intermediaire.question: Approximately how deep is the Dead Sea relative to sea level?
intermediaire.explanation: The Dead Sea is the lowest point on the earth's surface, approximately 430 m below sea level.

intermediaire.question: Which current country corresponds mainly to ancient Canaan?
options: Israel, Palestine, part of Lebanon and Jordan
intermediaire.explanation: Canaan roughly covered modern-day Israel, the Palestinian territories, part of Lebanon and Jordan.

intermediaire.question: On which mountain did Elijah confront the prophets of Baal?
intermediaire.explanation: Elijah challenged the 450 prophets of Baal at the foot of Mount Carmel, facing the Mediterranean (1 Kings 18).

intermediaire.question: In which city was Paul imprisoned for 2 years before going to Rome?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul was imprisoned for 2 years in Caesarea Maritime before Governor Felix, then Festus (Acts 24:27).

intermediaire.question: Which biblical city was known for its sacred prostitution and commerce, destroyed according to Revelation?
intermediaire.explanation: Babylon is the apocalyptic symbol of the ungodly city and unrighteous commerce (Revelation 18). Historically, several cities are suggested (Rome, Babylon).

intermediaire.question: In which desert was Jesus tempted for 40 days?
intermediaire.explanation: Tradition locates the temptation of Jesus in the Judean Desert, east of Jerusalem and Jericho.

intermediaire.question: What city was Paul's first port of call on his way from Jerusalem to Rome?
intermediaire.explanation: Antioch of Syria (via its port Seleucia) was the missionary base from which Paul set out on his travels (Acts 13:4).

intermediaire.question: In what geographic region was the city of Tarsus, Paul's homeland, located?
intermediaire.explanation: Tarsus is in Cilicia, in what is now southern Türkiye. Paul proudly referred to himself as 'a citizen of Tarsus' (Acts 21:39).

intermediaire.question: What is the literal Hebrew name for the Promised Land?
intermediaire.explanation: The Promised Land is referred to as 'Land of Canaan' (Eretz Kena'an) in the OT, after the name of its previous occupant.

intermediaire.question: By what route did the caravans cross Canaan in the OT?
options: Via Maris (Sea Way) along the coast
Route of the Patriarchs in the mountains
Royal road east of the Jordan
intermediaire.explanation: Three main routes: (1) Via Maris coastal; (2) Route of the Patriarchs (mountains); (3) Royal road east of Jordan — all mentioned in the OT.

intermediaire.question: Where were the 7 Churches receiving the Apocalypse?
intermediaire.explanation: The 7 Churches (Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea) were all in Asia Minor (Revelation 1:11).

intermediaire.question: In which city in Egypt did the Israelites build storehouse cities for Pharaoh?
intermediaire.explanation: The Israelites built the warehouse cities of Pithom and Ramesses for Pharaoh (Exodus 1:11).

intermediaire.question: What region of Egypt did Pharaoh assign to Jacob and his family?
intermediaire.explanation: Joseph settled his father and his brothers in the best land of Egypt, the land of Goshen (Genesis 47:6).

intermediaire.question: In which city did Joshua first establish the Tabernacle after the conquest of Canaan?
intermediaire.explanation: The whole congregation of Israel gathered together at Shiloh and pitched the Tent of Meeting there (Joshua 18:1).

intermediaire.question: In which city was the Ark of the Covenant placed with Abinadab after his return from the Philistines?
intermediaire.explanation: The people of Kirjath-jearim took the Ark into the house of Abinadab on the hill (1 Samuel 7:1).

intermediaire.question: Where did Solomon go at the beginning of his reign to offer a thousand burnt offerings and receive wisdom?
intermediaire.explanation: Solomon went to Gibeon to sacrifice, where the great high place and the brazen altar were (1 Kings 3:4-5).

intermediaire.question: Which two cities did Jeroboam I choose to install his golden calves?
intermediaire.explanation: To prevent the people from going up to Jerusalem, Jeroboam placed a golden calf in Bethel (south) and another in Dan (north) (1 Kings 12:29).

intermediaire.question: In which Phoenician city did Elijah stay with a widow during the famine?
intermediaire.explanation: God sent Elijah to Zarephath, a city belonging to Sidon, to a widow whose flour and oil were not lacking (1 Kings 17:9).

intermediaire.question: What was the royal summer residence of the kings of Israel where Naboth had his vineyard?
intermediaire.explanation: Naboth of Jezreel had a vineyard near Ahab's palace in Jezreel (1 Kings 21:1).

intermediaire.question: On which mountain did David mourn Saul and Jonathan, killed in battle?
intermediaire.explanation: Saul and his sons perished on Mount Gilboa against the Philistines (1 Samuel 31:1-8).

intermediaire.question: In what cave or desert region did David hide when he spared Saul's life?
intermediaire.explanation: David took refuge in the strongholds of Engedi near the Dead Sea, where he cut off a piece of Saul's cloak (1 Samuel 24).

intermediaire.question: In what precise place in the desert of Ethiopia or Palestine was the Ethiopian eunuch baptized by Philip?
options: On the deserted road from Jerusalem to Gaza
On the banks of the Nile
intermediaire.explanation: The angel sent Philip along the path that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza, a path that is deserted (Acts 8:26).

intermediaire.question: In which city in Macedonia did Paul convert Lydia and was thrown into prison with Silas?
intermediaire.explanation: In Philippi, the first Roman city in Macedonia visited by Paul, Lydia believed and a jailer converted after the earthquake (Acts 16).

intermediaire.question: Which people in a Macedonian town examined the Scriptures daily to verify Paul's words?
intermediaire.explanation: The Jews of Berea had nobler sentiments than those of Thessalonica and searched the Scriptures daily (Acts 17:11).

intermediaire.question: In which region of southeastern Judea is the city of Masada located?
intermediaire.explanation: The fortress of Masada overlooks the western shore of the Dead Sea.

intermediaire.question: What region northeast of the Jordan included a confederation of ten Hellenistic cities visited by Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: The Decapolis ('ten cities') extended mainly east of the Jordan and the Sea of ​​Galilee (Mark 5:20; 7:31).

intermediaire.question: In what area did Jesus heal the man possessed by 'Legion' and send the demons into a herd of swine?
options: The land of the Gadarenes / Gerasenes
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus crossed the Sea of ​​Galilee to the eastern shore, into the land of the Gerasenes/Gadarenites (Mark 5:1).

intermediaire.question: In which town in Phoenicia did Jesus heal the daughter of a Syrophoenician woman?
options: In the region of Tire and Sidon
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus withdrew to the territory of Tire and Sidon where he heard the faith of this woman (Mark 7:24-30).

intermediaire.question: Near which northern city, at the headwaters of the Jordan, did Peter confess that Jesus is the Christ?
intermediaire.explanation: It was in the villages of Caesarea Philippi, at the foot of Mount Hermon, that Peter made his confession (Matthew 16:13-16).

intermediaire.question: What river flowed near the city of Susa, where Nehemiah and Esther lived in the Persian court?
intermediaire.explanation: Daniel saw a vision in Shushan, in the province of Elam, by the river Ulai (Daniel 8:2).

intermediaire.question: In which city in Mesopotamia did Abraham live with his father Terah before entering Canaan?
intermediaire.explanation: Terah took Abram and Lot from Ur in Chaldea to Haran, from where Abraham departed to Canaan (Genesis 11:31-12:4).

intermediaire.question: Which biblical river traditionally marked the ideal northeastern boundary promised to Abraham?
intermediaire.explanation: God promised Abraham's descendants the land 'from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river of Euphrates' (Genesis 15:18).

intermediaire.question: Which city was the capital of the kingdom of Aram (Syria) in the Old Testament?
intermediaire.explanation: Damascus was the capital of Aram-Damascus, often in conflict or alliance with Israel (1 Kings 11:24; Isaiah 7:8).

intermediaire.question: In which street in Damascus did Saul of Tarsus regain his sight thanks to Ananias?
intermediaire.explanation: The Lord told Ananias to go to the street called Right, to the house of Judas (Acts 9:11).

intermediaire.question: Which Mediterranean island was the homeland of Barnabas and the first stop on the first missionary journey?
intermediaire.explanation: Barnabas was from Cyprus (Acts 4:36), where he and Paul landed at Salamis and crossed to Paphos (Acts 13).

intermediaire.question: In which province of Asia Minor were the cities of Iconium, Lystra and Derbe located?
intermediaire.explanation: Iconium, Lystra and Derbe belonged to the Roman province of South Galatia during Paul's first journey (Acts 14).

intermediaire.question: In which city were Paul and Barnabas mistaken for Zeus and Hermes after healing a lame man?
intermediaire.explanation: At Lystra, the crowd wanted to offer them sacrifices, calling them Zeus (Barnabas) and Hermes (Paul) (Acts 14:11-12).

intermediaire.question: Where did Ezekiel receive his visions among the Jewish exiles in Babylonia?
options: On the banks of the Nile
On the banks of the Kebar River
On the banks of the Jordan
intermediaire.explanation: Ezekiel was among the captives near the Chebar River (a channel of the Euphrates) when the heavens opened (Ezekiel 1:1).

intermediaire.question: Which city in the far north of Israel gave the biblical expression 'from Dan to ___'?
intermediaire.explanation: 'From Dan to Beersheba' meant the whole extent of Israel, from the extreme north to the south of the Negev (Judges 20:1).

intermediaire.question: What arid desert lies south of Judea around Beersheba?
intermediaire.explanation: The Negev ('dry/south') is the semi-desert region where Abraham and Isaac lived around Beersheba (Genesis 20:1).

intermediaire.question: Which coastal city was built by Herod the Great and became the Roman administrative capital of Judea?
intermediaire.explanation: Caesarea Maritime was home to Roman prefects and procurators such as Pilate, Felix, and Festus (Acts 23:23).

intermediaire.question: In which city did Herod the Great build Herodion's palace-fortress and was he buried?
intermediaire.explanation: Herodium is an artificial hill located about 12 km south of Jerusalem, near Bethlehem.

intermediaire.question: What river separates Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives?
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus crossed the Kidron River with his disciples to the Garden of Gethsemane (John 18:1).

intermediaire.question: Near which stream did Jacob struggle all night with a stranger before finding Esau?
intermediaire.explanation: Jacob crossed the Jabbok (eastern tributary of the Jordan) and there received the name Israel (Genesis 32:22-28).

intermediaire.question: Which high snow-capped mountain marks the northern border of Israel?
intermediaire.explanation: Mount Hermon (2,814 m) dominates northern Israel and feeds the sources of the Jordan (Psalm 133:3).

intermediaire.question: What port on the island of Crete did Paul recommend using to overwinter before shipwreck (Acts 27:8-12)?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul warned against returning to sea from Beaux-Ports in Crete, but the centurion preferred to try to reach Phoenix.

intermediaire.question: In which port city in Asia Minor did Paul bid a moving farewell to the elders of Ephesus (Acts 20)?
intermediaire.explanation: To save time in Asia, Paul brought the elders from Ephesus to Miletus (Acts 20:17).

intermediaire.question: In which port did Paul see the vision of the Macedonian man who begged him: 'Go to Macedonia, help us!' ?
intermediaire.explanation: It was at Troas, on the Aegean coast, that Paul received the call to Europe (Acts 16:8-10).

intermediaire.question: What were the two ports that served Corinth, making it a major commercial crossroads?
intermediaire.explanation: Located on the isthmus, Corinth connected the Gulf of Corinth (Lechaion) and the Saronic Gulf (Cenchreae, cited in Romans 16:1).

intermediaire.question: What was the name of the port where Paul landed in Italy before returning to Rome (Acts 28:13)?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul landed at Pozzuoli, in the Bay of Naples, where he already found Christian brothers (Acts 28:13-14).

intermediaire.question: Which city was the capital of the kingdom of Edom southeast of the Dead Sea (often identified with the cliffs of Petra/Sela)?
intermediaire.explanation: Edom occupied the mountains of Seir with strongholds like Botzra and Selah (2 Kings 14:7; Obadiah).

intermediaire.question: On which plain did Ezekiel see the valley of dry bones?
options: A valley/plain in Babylonia (often connected to the Kebar River)
intermediaire.explanation: The Spirit carried Ezekiel into the middle of a valley filled with bones in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 37:1).

intermediaire.question: Which northern Canaanite city was burned by Joshua after his victory over King Jabin (Joshua 11)?
intermediaire.explanation: Hazor, which was 'the capital of all these kingdoms,' was taken and burned by Joshua (Joshua 11:10-11).

intermediaire.question: In which Philistine city did the Ark of the Covenant bring down the statue of the god Dagon?
intermediaire.explanation: The Philistines placed the Ark in the temple of Dagon in Ashdod, where the idol collapsed before it (1 Samuel 5:1-4).

intermediaire.question: Which hometown of Goliath was one of the five cities of the Philistine pentapolis?
intermediaire.explanation: Goliath was from Gath (1 Samuel 17:4); the five cities were Gaza, Ashdod, Ascalon, Gath and Ekron.

intermediaire.question: In which mountainous region were Shiloh, Bethel and Jerusalem located?
options: The central highlands (mountain of Ephraim and Judah)
intermediaire.explanation: The central mountain ridge is home to most of the great sanctuaries and historic cities of the OT.

intermediaire.question: In which city in Judea was John the Baptist probably born according to tradition (house of Zechariah and Elizabeth)?
options: A town in the mountain of Judah (traditionally Ein Kerem)
intermediaire.explanation: Luke 1:39 records that Mary went with haste into the hill country to a town in Judah (identified as Ein Kerem).

intermediaire.question: In which city in the Acts of the Apostles did Philip the deacon preach successfully before the arrival of Peter and John?
intermediaire.explanation: Philip went down to a town in Samaria and proclaimed Christ there with many signs (Acts 8:5-14).

expert.question: What is the geographical significance of the concept of 'Promised Land' in Covenant theology?
options: Symbol of divine heritage, place of the presence of God and prefiguration of eschatological rest
Territory conquered by military force alone
expert.explanation: The Earth (eretz) is in biblical theology: place of the divine Presence, fulfillment of the promise to Abraham, and prefiguration of the eschatological heritage (Hebrews 11:10,16).

expert.question: What is the theological significance of Jerusalem as the 'navel of the world' (Ezekiel 38:12)?
options: The centrality of Jerusalem in the divine plan as a meeting place between heaven and earth, God and humanity
A concept developed only in the NT
expert.explanation: The 'center of the earth' (tabbur ha-aretz) in Ezekiel 38:12 expresses the theological and eschatological centrality of Jerusalem in the divine plan.

expert.question: What is the precise geographical route of Paul's first missionary journey according to Acts?
options: Antioch → Cyprus → Perge → Antioch of Pisidia → Iconium → Lystra → Derbe → return
expert.explanation: 1st journey (Acts 13-14): Antioch → Seleucia → Cyprus (Salamis, Paphos) → Perge → Antioch of Pisidia → Iconium → Lystra → Derbe → return.

expert.question: What was the geopolitical significance of Canaan between Egypt and Mesopotamia?
options: An isolated territory of no importance
A strategic corridor between the two great empires, a place of passage and constant conflicts
An agricultural region without military issues
expert.explanation: Canaan was the 'land bridge' between Egypt and Mesopotamia — its strategic position explains the numerous invasions and successive domination by the great empires.

expert.question: In what eschatological perspective does Zechariah describe the geographical transformation of Jerusalem (Zechariah 14)?
options: The Mount of Olives will be split, Jerusalem will be lifted up, and living waters will flow east and west.
A vision of the historical past
expert.explanation: Zechariah 14 describes an eschatological transformation: the Mount of Olives split (v.4), Jerusalem lifted up (v.10), living waters flowing to the two seas (v.8).

expert.question: What is the symbolic meaning of the Jordan in biblical theology?
options: Symbol of transformative passage: from slavery to freedom (Exodus), from wandering to inheritance (Joshua), from sin to grace (baptism)
A sacred river without symbolic significance
expert.explanation: The Jordan crosses the great biblical moments: crossing on dry ground (Joshua 3-4), baptism of Jesus, healing of Naaman — symbol of transformative passages.

expert.question: What is the relationship between the geography of the creation story (Genesis 2) and the rivers of Eden?
options: Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel (Tiger) and Phrat (Euphrates) suggest a location in Mesopotamia, but the text has a cosmological significance
Rivers exclusively represent the 4 cardinal points
expert.explanation: Genesis 2:10-14: Tigris and Euphrates are identifiable. Pishon and Gihon are debated. The text has both a geographical and cosmological scope (the garden as a cosmic temple).

expert.question: Why was the city of Ephesus strategically important to the Pauline mission?
options: Capital of the province of Asia, major commercial and religious crossroads, center of the cult of Artemis — an ideal base for evangelizing all of Asia
Paul only stayed there for a few days
expert.explanation: Paul stayed in Ephesus for 3 years (Acts 19-20). A commercial and religious crossroads, Ephesus provided access to all of Asia Minor.

expert.question: What is the significance of the 'Road of the Patriarchs' in the geography of Genesis?
options: The north-south axis in the mountainous area of ​​Canaan (Beer-Sheva, Hebron, Bethel, Shechem) marking the places of alliance of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
expert.explanation: The patriarchs follow an axis in the heights of Canaan: Beersheba (covenant) → Hebron (burial) → Bethel (vision) → Shechem (altar) — each step marks an act of alliance.

expert.question: How does the geography of Revelation (Babylon vs New Jerusalem) structure its theology?
options: These are two future physical cities
Two cities symbolize two opposing spiritual systems: Babylon (idolatrous and oppressive empire) vs New Jerusalem (city of God and the Lamb)
Simple Roman political allegory without theological significance
expert.explanation: The Apocalypse opposes two symbolic 'cities': Babylon (Rev 17-18) = system of the world opposed to God; New Jerusalem (Rev 21-22) = the perfect city of the divine presence.

expert.question: What is the symbolic meaning of the desert (midbar) in biblical theology?
options: Place of testing, encounter with God, spiritual formation and divine engagement (Hosea 2:14)
Exclusive symbol of death and judgment
expert.explanation: The 'midbar' (desert) is ambivalent: a place of temptation AND of intimate divine encounter. Hosea 2:14: 'I will lead her into the wilderness and speak to her heart.'

expert.question: What is the theological significance of the 'ascent to Jerusalem' in the synoptic gospels?
options: An eschatological and sacrificial climb: Jesus deliberately goes up to Jerusalem to fulfill his passion (Luke 9:51: 'he made the decision to walk towards Jerusalem')
expert.explanation: The 'ascent' to Jerusalem is a central theological motif (Luke 9:51-19:44): Jesus ascends as the Suffering Servant to the place of sacrifice, resurrection and inauguration of the Kingdom.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the name 'Babylon' in 1 Peter 5:13 and its actual geographical context?
options: The real city of Babylon in Mesopotamia
A cryptic name for Rome, as in Revelation — common usage in post-70 AD Jewish literature. AD
expert.explanation: Almost all historians identify 'Babylon' in 1 Peter 5:13 with Rome. Similar usage in Revelation and post-70s Jewish literature to designate the oppressive empire.

expert.question: Which valley located southwest of Jerusalem (Ge-Hinnom) gave its name to the term 'Gehenna'?
expert.explanation: The valley of Ben-Hinnom, scene of pagan sacrifices under Ahaz and Manasseh, became the symbol of the final judgment (Gehenna).

expert.question: What geographic term refers to the low hills between the Philistine coastal plain and the mountains of Judah?
expert.explanation: The Shephelah ('lowlands') was a strategic buffer zone with fortresses like Lachish, Azekah and Beth-Shemesh.

expert.question: Which Shephelah fortress was besieged by Sennacherib in 701 BC? AD, scene immortalized on the bas-reliefs of Nineveh?
expert.explanation: The bas-reliefs of Sennacherib's palace in Nineveh accurately depict the siege of Lachish in 701 BC. AD

expert.question: What fertile valley or plain in northern Israel connects the Mediterranean coast to the Jordan River and serves as a symbol of 'Armageddon'?
options: The plain of Jezreel (Esdrelon), dominated by Megiddo
expert.explanation: Armageddon comes from 'Har-Megiddo' (mountain of Megiddo), which commands access to the strategic plain of Jezreel (Revelation 16:16).

expert.question: What fertile plateau east of Lake Galilee was famous for its oaks and great bulls in the OT?
expert.explanation: Bashan was known for its oak trees (Isaiah 2:13) and vigorous flocks (Psalm 22:13; Amos 4:1).

expert.question: What river marked the border between the territories of Edom/Moab or between Moab and the Amorites?
expert.explanation: The torrent of the Arnon, a deep canyon flowing into the Dead Sea, separated Moab from the Amorite kingdom of Sihon (Numbers 21:13).

expert.question: What is the geographical identification of the 'river of Egypt' (Nahal Mitzraim) in several borders of the AT?
expert.explanation: In the texts describing the southern border of Canaan (Numbers 34:5; Joshua 15:4), 'the torrent of Egypt' refers to Wadi el-Arish.

expert.question: Which tectonic depression extends from Lake Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba via the Dead Sea?
expert.explanation: The great Rift divide (Jordan valley and Araba) goes down to -430 m at the Dead Sea before joining the Red Sea.

expert.question: Which 533 meter hydraulic tunnel dug under Hezekiah connected the spring of Gihon to the pool of Siloam?
expert.explanation: Excavated by two teams starting from opposite ends around 701 BC. BC, it ensured water to Jerusalem during the Assyrian siege (2 Chronicles 32:30).

expert.question: What international trade route ran along the Mediterranean coast then through Megiddo to Damascus?
options: The Via Maris ('Way of the Sea')
expert.explanation: The Via Maris connected Egypt to Syria and Mesopotamia via the coastal plain, Megiddo and Galilee (Isaiah 9:1).

expert.question: Where was Étsion-Géber, the seaport used by Solomon's fleet?
options: On the Mediterranean coast near Gaza
At the bottom of the Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea), near Elat
expert.explanation: Solomon built a fleet at Etzion-geber, near Eloth, on the banks of the Red Sea (1 Kings 9:26).

expert.question: Which biblical region corresponds to the current coastal plain between Jaffa and Mount Carmel?
expert.explanation: The plain of Sharon was famous for its fertility and flowers (Song 2:1; Isaiah 35:2).

expert.question: What were the names of the 6 special cities spread across the Jordan to protect against involuntary manslaughter?
options: Cities of refuge (Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron, Betser, Ramoth, Golan)
expert.explanation: God established six cities of refuge—three west and three east of the Jordan—accessible quickly from throughout the land (Joshua 20:7-8).

expert.question: Which site in the Judean Desert, northwest of the Dead Sea, was home to the community that copied the biblical scrolls?
expert.explanation: The caves of Khirbet Qumran yielded the Dead Sea Scrolls between 1947 and 1956.

expert.question: Which city in the Apocalypse was known for its warm water from aqueducts (unlike the hot springs of Hierapolis and the cold springs of Colossae)?
expert.explanation: The allusion to water being neither cold nor boiling in Revelation 3:15-16 directly reflects Laodicea's supply of lukewarm water.

expert.question: Which city among the 7 Churches of Revelation was home to a famous monumental altar of Zeus ('the throne of Satan')?
expert.explanation: Pergamum (Revelation 2:13) had the great altar of Zeus on its acropolis as well as an early imperial cult.

expert.question: Which city in Asia Minor, recipient of the Apocalypse, was famous for its purple dye works (homeland of Lydia)?
expert.explanation: Lydia, a purple merchant whom Paul met in Philippi, was from Thyatira (Acts 16:14; Revelation 2:18).

expert.question: On which Roman road was Paul escorted by the brothers who came from Rome to the 'Forum of Appius' and the 'Three Taverns'?
expert.explanation: The Via Appia linked southern Italy to Rome; Christians came to meet Paul at these two relay points (Acts 28:15).

expert.question: Which Roman road crossed Macedonia from east to west, connecting Philippi, Thessalonica and the Adriatic Sea?
expert.explanation: Paul took the Via Egnatia on his 2nd missionary journey from Neapolis/Philippes to Thessalonica (Acts 16-17).

expert.question: What was the name of the temple built by the Samaritans as a rival to that of Jerusalem?
expert.explanation: John 4:20 refers to this sanctuary on Mount Gerizim ('Our fathers worshiped on this mountain').

expert.question: In which northern royal city did Omri establish his new capital around 880 BC? AD on a hill purchased in Shemer?
expert.explanation: Omri purchased the hill of Shemer and built Samaria there, which remained the capital of the Northern Kingdom until 722 BC. (1 Kings 16:24).

expert.question: Which city was the ancient capital of Judah before Jerusalem, and the place of the tombs of the patriarchs (Makpelah)?
expert.explanation: Abraham purchased the cave of Makpelah in Hebron (Genesis 23), where Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah were buried.

expert.question: Where in the Temple of Jerusalem did the curtain (veil) separate the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies?
options: In the courts of the pagans
expert.explanation: The veil separating the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies was torn from top to bottom at the death of Jesus (Mark 15:38).

expert.question: Which Jerusalem gate or pool, with five porticos near the Sheep Gate, is mentioned in John 5?
expert.explanation: Archaeological excavations near St. Anne's in Jerusalem confirmed the two pools surrounded by five porticos of Bethesda (John 5:2).

expert.question: Which covered portico of the Temple in Jerusalem served as a gathering place for the early Christians (Acts 5:12)?
expert.explanation: Solomon's portico, on the eastern side of the Temple esplanade, hosted the teaching of Jesus (John 10:23) and then the apostles.

expert.question: In which region of Egypt did a Jewish military colony have its own Yahwist temple in the 5th century BC? AD?
expert.explanation: The Elephantine papyri reveal the existence of a Jewish community on an island in the Nile on the southern border of Egypt.

expert.question: Which city located on the eastern bank of the Jordan served as a refuge for the Christians of Jerusalem before the siege of 70 AD? BC according to Eusebius?
expert.explanation: According to Eusebius of Caesarea, Christians fled Jerusalem to Pella in Perea/Decapolis before the destruction in 70.

expert.question: Which biblical region corresponds to central Transjordan, attributed to the tribes of Reuben and Gad?
options: Gilead and the plain of Moab
expert.explanation: The land of Gilead, mountainous and wooded east of the Jordan, was divided between Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 32).

expert.question: What desert lies directly east of Jerusalem down toward Jericho and the Dead Sea?
expert.explanation: The Judean Desert drops abruptly from +800 m in Jerusalem to -430 m at the Dead Sea over around thirty kilometers.

expert.question: Which Nabataean city controlled the incense routes to southeastern Israel in NT times (kingdom of Aretas IV, 2 Cor 11:32)?
expert.explanation: Paul mentions the Nabataean king Aretas IV who guarded Damascus (2 Corinthians 11:32).

expert.question: Which port on the Lycian coast allowed Paul to change ships to an Alexandrian vessel en route to Rome (Acts 27:5-6)?
expert.explanation: At Myra in Lycia, the centurion Julius found a ship from Alexandria sailing towards Italy.

expert.question: Which city was the port of Antioch in Syria from where Paul and Barnabas sailed to Cyprus?
expert.explanation: They went down to Seleucia, a seaport of Antioch at the mouth of the Orontes, and from there sailed to Cyprus (Acts 13:4).

expert.question: Which island in the Aegean Sea served as Paul's first European stopover before Neapolis?
expert.explanation: Departing from Troas, they headed straight for Samothrace, and the next day for Neapolis (Acts 16:11).

expert.question: What was the port of Philippi where Paul landed in Europe?
expert.explanation: Neapolis served as a port for the Roman colony of Philippi, located about 15 km inland (Acts 16:11-12).

expert.question: Which mountainous region of Israel is home to the cities of Nazareth, Cana and Mount Tabor?
expert.explanation: The Lower Galilee, with fertile valleys and moderate hills, concentrates the majority of evangelical sites around Nazareth and Tiberias.

expert.question: What a new city founded by Herod Antipas around 20 AD? J.-C. gave its other name to Lake Galilee?
expert.explanation: Named in honor of the emperor Tiberius, Tiberias gave its name to the 'Sea of ​​Tiberias' in the Gospel of John (John 6:1; 21:1).

expert.question: Which galactic capital of Herod Antipas, located just 6 km north of Nazareth, is never named in the Gospels?
expert.explanation: Zipphoris was a large Greco-Roman city neighboring Nazareth, where Joseph and Jesus carpenters were able to work, although not mentioned in the NT.

expert.question: Where was the place called 'Ainon, near Salim', where John baptized because there was plenty of water (John 3:23)?
expert.explanation: Aïnon ('sources') near Salim was located in the Jordan valley rich in abundant springs.

expert.question: Which fortress city east of the Dead Sea was the place of the imprisonment and beheading of John the Baptist according to Flavius ​​Josephus?
expert.explanation: Flavius ​​Josephus (Antiquities 18.5.2) places the execution of John the Baptist by Herod Antipas in the fortress of Machaerus in Perea.

expert.question: Which river in Mesopotamia borders ancient Nineveh, capital of the Assyrian Empire?
expert.explanation: Nineveh stood on the eastern bank of the Tigris, facing modern-day Mosul in Iraq.

expert.question: On which river did the ancient city of Babylon stand?
expert.explanation: The Euphrates flowed through the heart of the city of Babylon (Psalm 137:1: 'On the banks of the rivers of Babylon').

expert.question: Which biblical region located south of Judea between Hebron and the Negev was Esau's territory after the departure from Edom?
expert.explanation: The Edomites settled in southern Judah after the exile, giving rise to Idumea, from which Herod the Great came (Mark 3:8).

expert.question: In which city in Egypt did a large Jewish community translate the Hebrew Bible into Greek (Septuagint)?
expert.explanation: Alexandria, founded by Alexander the Great, was home to the largest Hellenic-speaking Jewish diaspora in the ancient world.

expert.question: Which city in Greece located in Achaia was the seat of a turbulent Church to which Paul wrote at least two long epistles?
expert.explanation: Corinth was the capital of the Roman province of Achaia, where Paul stayed for 18 months (Acts 18:1-11).

expert.question: Which island in the eastern Mediterranean is associated with Titus in the epistle addressed to him?
expert.explanation: Paul left Titus in Crete to finish organizing the churches and establishing elders in each city (Titus 1:5).

expert.question: Which Roman province in Asia Minor brought together the Churches of Colossae, Laodicea and Hierapolis in the Lycos valley?
expert.explanation: Colossae, Laodicea, and Hierapolis formed a triad of neighboring cities in the Lycus Valley of Phrygia (Colossians 4:13).

expert.question: What historic mountain pass or pass connected the coastal plain to Jerusalem, where Joshua stopped the sun (Joshua 10)?
options: The valley of Ayalon / rise of Beth-horon
expert.explanation: Joshua pursued the Amorite kings up Beth Horon toward the Valley of Ayalon (Joshua 10:10-12).

expert.question: What location east of Jericho marked Israel's last encampment before crossing the Jordan?
expert.explanation: The Israelites camped on the plains of Moab at Shittim opposite Jericho before crossing the Jordan (Numbers 22:1; Joshua 3:1).
